name: LayoutKit
baseline: Auto Layout (NSLayoutConstraint) laying out self-sizing UICollectionView cells
verdict_reason: LinkedIn's claim that LayoutKit matches manual layout and beats Auto Layout still holds on current hardware: an independent 2025 run puts it 3.8x-3.9x ahead of Auto Layout and slightly ahead of manual frame code. The project itself has been archived since 2021.
tier_reason: Numbers come from layoutBox's public LayoutFrameworkBenchmark (not LinkedIn), with device, iOS version and Release mode stated; LinkedIn's own benchmark page is chart-only.
claimed_speedup: LinkedIn: 'as fast as manual layout code and ... significantly faster than Auto Layout' (chart only, iPhone 6, iOS 9.3.2). Independent run, 100 cells: iPhone 16 0.0156 s vs 0.0595 s Auto Layout (3.8x, derived from page data) and 0.0208 s manual; iPhone 13 Pro iOS 18.6 0.0165 s vs 0.064 s Auto Layout (3.9x, derived from page data) and 0.0216 s manual.
workload: Lay out a feed-style UICollectionView cell for 10 to 100 cells per pass; seconds for vc.view.layoutIfNeeded() on the main thread.
os: iOS 18.6 (iPhone 13 Pro); iPhone 16 OS not stated; LinkedIn's original iOS 9.3.2
toolchain: Release mode per LayoutFrameworkBenchmark README; LinkedIn ran 'with Swift optimization turned on'
platforms: iOS, macOS, tvOS (last release targets Swift 4-era toolchains)
one_liner: LinkedIn's immutable layout engine for UIKit; still about 3.8x faster than Auto Layout in a 2025 run, but archived since 2021.
how_it_is_fast: Layouts are immutable value descriptions that compute frames directly, without a constraint solver. Because the result is plain data, it can be computed on a background thread and cached, then applied to views on the main thread.
use_it_when: Studying or forking a proven background-thread layout design for feed cells
Legacy codebases that already depend on it
skip_it_when: New projects: the repository is archived and receives no fixes for new Swift or iOS releases
caveats: LinkedIn's own benchmark page is chart-only and dates from iOS 9.3.2 on an iPhone 6.
The independent numbers measure main-thread layout of one synthetic feed cell, not LayoutKit's background precomputation.
Archived by LinkedIn (now under LinkedInAttic); last commit 2021-02-17.
tradeoffs: Views are described through LayoutKit's own layout types rather than UIKit constraints.
No maintenance: future Swift language modes and SDKs may break the build.

evidence.quote: LayoutKit is as fast as manual layout code and is [significantly faster than Auto Layout]
Benchmarks were run on an iPhone 6 running iOS 9.3.2 with Swift optimization turned on.
